issues.problem: T06's core premise — that pre-push-hook.md contains no contradicted claim — is false. pre-push-hook.md line 17 says cpus is "env-driven (`BUILD_CPUS`, default 1 — only the VPS deploy sets it to 4)". next.config.js lines 64-66 read `cpus: (isVercel || isCI || process.env.SELF_HOSTED) ? split_quality: The heldout four are genuinely harder than the iteration six — each carries a real trap (blanket deferral T07, false-positive from a declared-but-unused dependency T08, the degenerate all-unverifiable answer T09, non-activation T10) and none is a straightforward find-the-drift exercise. But the set is narrow: T07, T08 and T09 all discriminate on the same underlying axis, resisting unwarranted deferral or unwarranted findings, while the two priority qualities about diagnosing which side is wrong and proposing actionable corrections (contract ranks 5 and 6) are held entirely in the iteration split. T06 is also a near-twin of the heldout T08, so the obeyed-without-fabrication pattern is pre-taught during iteration. Recommended repair in B16: swap T02 into heldout and T08 into iteration, giving a heldout set that spans four distinct axes rather than two.
bias_verdict: No task or packet rewards the original's surface habits — the C1-C8/U1-U6 check-ID scheme, the emoji status vocabulary, the two-pass report template and the accepted-debt mechanism are all absent from the suite, and every packet's not_quality block explicitly discounts severity vocabulary and presentation. The stale-vs-violated taxonomy the suite leans on is contract-derived (never_do[5], objective_invariant[3]), not borrowed from the original's compliance/currency passes. Nor is anything visibly engineered to make the original fail; T07/T08/T09 target rule files the original has no scripted check for, but generalising beyond CLAUDE.md is squarely inside the contract's scope_in. The real bias is by omission and it runs pro-original: the three contract clauses the original most plainly breaches — editing and committing during the audit (Step 5), silently skipping rules listed in accepted-debt.md (Step 2), and emitting a status-symbol scorecard in place of findings (Step 4, scope_out[6]) — are the three the benchmark never tests. Whether or not that was deliberate, the suite cannot currently distinguish an implementation that respects the read-only and no-silent-drop constraints from one that does not. Adding the B3 and B4 tasks removes the shielding.
